claim: The follow-up panel and the screen disagree on the same lipids at the same stated dose in the same cell line.
locus_a: Source Data MOESM4 sheet 'Fig. 2b'/'Fig. 2c' (initial screen, HepG2, 15 ng mRNA per 5,000 cells, 24 h, n=2): 12T-O14 mean 241,938; 15T-O16 mean 459,052; 13T-O12 mean 237,150.
locus_b: Source Data MOESM4 sheet 'Fig. 2g' ('In vitro transfection of top 8 AID-LNPs', 15 ng arm, n=2): 12T-O14 mean 129,281; 15T-O16 mean 147,130; 13T-O12 mean 218,752.
what_we_emitted: The SCREEN values only (05_values.csv). Fig. 2g is not emitted.
why: The eight lipids common to both run 0.32x-0.95x of their screen values, geometric mean 0.64x, and their RANKS do not survive: Spearman = -0.262 (p=0.53, n=8), Pearson on log10 = -0.062, while the screen's own two replicates agree at Spearman 0.990 over all 100 lipids. 15T-O16 is 1st of 8 in the screen and 7th of 8 in the follow-up. Neither caption states a formulation or protocol difference -- Fig. 2b's own subtitle and Supplementary Fig. 2's caption both give 15 ng and HepG2 -- so the paper offers no stated reason for the shift. This is a same-lab, same-assay, cross-experiment reproducibility fact and it is the single most load-bearing thing in this curation for the project's Result 3; it is recorded here rather than averaged away.

claim: A compound is named two different ways in the caption and in its own Source Data.
locus_a: Supplementary Fig. 6 caption, MOESM1 p.9: 'Synthesis of 12T-O18a and 12T-O18b and comparison of their mRNA delivery efficiency with 12T-O14'.
locus_b: Source Data MOESM3 sheet 'Fig. S6', row 5: '12T-18a', '12T-18b' (the 'O' of the acrylate token dropped).
what_we_emitted: Neither. These two are not library members and are not emitted.
why: The library's naming convention is <amine>T-O<tail carbons>, so '12T-18a' parses as tail '18a' with no O, which is not a token the library defines. QC check P13 lists exactly these two as the only unresolved names in the whole Source Data set. Recorded so that a later join on lipid name does not silently drop or mis-key them.

claim: The relative hit rate for one acrylate tail is stored at a different precision from the other three.
locus_a: Source Data MOESM4 sheet 'Fig. 2f', column D: O9 = -16.3, O14 = 9.8, O16 = 5.4 (one decimal).
locus_b: Same sheet, same column: O12 = 1 (an integer cell).
what_we_emitted: Our computed value, 1.087, is recorded in 07_qc.json P8 alongside the stored 1.
why: Recomputing the quantity as (share of the 23 outstanding lipids) - (share of the 100-member library) reproduces eight of the nine printed values to within 0.02; O12's stored 1 is 0.087 away, which is the rounding of 1.087 to zero decimals. Small, but it is the only one of nine that is not exact and absorbing it silently into a tolerance is how a real 1-in-9 defect would be hidden.

claim: The in-vitro dose is stated in two units that are only equivalent under an unstated assumption.
locus_a: Fig. 2b panel subtitle: '15 ng mRNA per 5,000 cells'.
locus_b: Supplementary Fig. 2 caption, MOESM1 p.4: 'HepG2 cells were treated with mLuc-loaded AID-LNPs at a dose of 15 ng mRNA/well'. Supplementary Figs. 3, 4, 6 and 10 repeat 'per well'.
what_we_emitted: Both strings, verbatim, in 05_values.csv's `dose` field as '15 ng mRNA per 5,000 cells'.
why: The two agree only if a well was seeded with 5,000 cells, which neither the SI nor any figure caption we hold states; the Methods section is in the main article, which is subscription-restricted (00_value_sources.json). The per-cell normalisation matters for any cross-paper comparison of absolute luminescence, so the assumption is recorded rather than resolved.

claim: The paper is not consistent about whether the ring-alkyl aniline is the head or the tail of the lipid.
locus_a: Abstract: 'identification of a tail-like amine-ring-alkyl aniline that generally affords efficacious lipids'.
locus_b: Supplementary discussion, MOESM1 p.35: 'we discovered ring-alkyl aniline as a superior head (or tail) that can generally yield efficacious lipids'.
what_we_emitted: No head/tail decomposition at all. 03_enumerated.csv stores whole-molecule SMILES and 01_blocks.csv keeps the amine and the acrylate as what they are: the two reagents.
why: Head/tail is a modelling convention, not a measurement, and this paper's own authors decline to commit. Any corpus column that forces one would be recording our choice as theirs. Flagged so that a later decomposition step does not invent an assignment.

claim: The same group of amines carries two different names in two adjacent panels.
locus_a: Fig. 2d, dashed box: 'Long-chain alkylamines', spanning amines 3-6.
locus_b: Source Data MOESM4 sheet 'Fig. 2e', column B header: 'C14-18 alkylamine'.
what_we_emitted: Neither name. The group is identified in 07_qc.json P9 by its members (amines 3-6) and by their measured chain lengths (14, 16, 18, 18).
why: Not an error, and in fact useful: the second name encodes chain lengths the paper never tabulates, which is what makes P9 an external test of the pixel measurement. Recorded because the two labels name the same four amines and a reader meeting only one of them would not know that.

claim: The library is used unpurified, and the paper shows the purified material is not always the same.
locus_a: Supplementary Fig. 5, MOESM1 p.7: 'Selected AID-lipids were purified using a CombiFlash NextGen 300+ chromatography system' -- i.e. the screened material was not purified.
locus_b: Source Data MOESM3 sheet 'Fig. S5': 12T-O14 unpurified 24.48e6 / 22.54e6 vs purified 30.10e6 / 20.25e6; 13T-O14 unpurified 18.22e6 / 17.68e6 vs purified 13.00e6 / 17.00e6; 12T-O16 unpurified 752e3 / 1001e3 vs purified 650e3 / 900e3.
what_we_emitted: The structures as the pure intended products, with no flag for crude content.
why: Every value in 05_values.csv was measured on a crude one-pot reaction mixture, not on an isolated compound, so the stored SMILES is the intended product rather than the sole species present. The paper's own purified-vs-unpurified comparison (n=2, 5 lipids, i.m. in vivo) spans 0.81x-1.23x and does not separate them, which is why this is recorded as a property of the dataset rather than flagged per row.
